mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer demand for residential construction, which typically precedes increased corporate investment and consumer spending, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises month-over-month, or the rank correlation between HOUST and 20-day returns falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity, causing S&P 500 forward returns to decline over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for three months, or the rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 5-day returns is negative in the tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS growth) combined with tight monetary policy (FEDFUNDS above 2.0%) indicates an overheating economy, which triggers a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the interaction condition, or the rank IC between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO below 95.0 for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 tends to decline in the following 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings from industrial sectors.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 95.0 for two months, or the rank IC between INDPRO and returns in the slowdown regime is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates accelerating inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month, or the rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to lower consumer spending and corporate profits, causing S&P 500 forward returns to decline over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two months, or the rank IC between UNRATE and returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with a manufacturing slowdown (INDPRO below 95.0) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the interaction condition, or the rank IC between the interaction signal and returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a consumer spending slowdown (RSAFS growth below 0.2% for three months), the S&P 500 tends to decline in the following 5 trading days as retail sector weakness signals reduced corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS growth is below 0.2% for three months, or the rank IC between RSAFS and returns in the slowdown regime is negative.
